title: California’s Tallest and Most Iconic Trees Are Getting Heatstroke
summary:
A grove of coast redwood trees is a forest of forests.
This means trees are slowing their “breathing” and “eating” because they can’t cool down fast enough when temperatures rise.
Trees use the pores in their leaves, stomata, to do two things: take carbon dioxide in, and let water out.
Open stomata mean the tree is “breathing” in carbon dioxide and photosynthesizing, but probably also letting water out.
Closed stomata mean the tree is conserving water but also slowing down its photosynthesis, since it isn’t taking in any carbon dioxide.

title: UK launches flood taskforce to prepare for extreme winter weather
summary:
The government has launched a new taskforce to respond to extreme weather, including the risk of flooding this winter.
"We're facing extreme weather, with flood and drought intertwined but the government is taking decisive action," Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) Minister Emma Hardy said in a statement ahead of the meeting.
Defra will host the first meeting on Wednesday, bringing together the Met Office, Environment Agency and mayoral authorities as well as the farming, water and insurance industries.
It has urged households to check their flood risk, sign up to alerts and make a flood plan to prepare for any emergencies.
The warnings follow 12 months of extreme weather across the UK, with the summer of 2026 the country's hottest on record.

title: Surrey County Council exceeds its tree planting target
summary:
More than 800,000 new trees have been planted across Surrey over the past five years, exceeding the council's own target, according to a report.
Surrey County Council's report found 116,359 trees had been planted in the 2025/26 financial year alone.
It said the total planted between 2021 and 2026 was around 885,000, surpassing its initial target of 600,000.
However, Elmbridge Borough Council recently passed a motion calling for the future East Surrey council to update its tree strategy to consider survival rates.
It said many trees planted in the borough were dying within a year as a result of not receiving the right aftercare.

title: Forever chemicals at former Oxfordshire fuel depot 'have been removed'
summary:
Barrels of chemicals left at an approved development site have been removed and testing carried out, a developer has said.
The Islip Fuel Depot in Oxfordshire is a former RAF and Esso fuel storage and transfer facility and has had outline planning permission approved to build residential and affordable homes.
Concerns were raised after campaigners discovered about 40 barrels of firefighting foam liquid, which contains PFAS - a group of chemicals often dubbed forever chemicals, had been left at the site for decades.
Developer, Newcore, said it had already identified the potential contamination and that "this potential risk and any contamination identified will be cleaned up immediately."
The depot previously supplied fuel to the former RAF Upper Heyford, around five miles north, which is suspected to be the source of forever chemical, or PFAS, contamination from firefighting foam.

title: Fired Government Scientists Are Finding New Ways to Spread the Word on Climate Change
summary:
In April of last year, Donald Trump’s administration halted work on a climate science report that the United States had been producing for over 20 years.
The congressionally mandated National Climate Assessment (NCA) is meant to give Americans a clear view of how climate change is impacting the nation.
Now, many of these scientists have released the first of a series of reports meant to look at how climate research has progressed since the last NCA in 2023, and where climate research could go next.

title: Homes and bridges swept away as fresh floods hit Nepal
summary:
A major river in Nepal has flooded, sweeping away houses, bridges and damaging a part of hydropower station, authorities have said.
A video of the flood shows the moment raging waters sweep down a valley and wash away an entire building complex.
The flood swept away about a dozen houses and several suspension bridges, while a hydroelectric project was damaged, carrying some of the construction equipment away, the disaster management authority said.
